## v0.1.29 — `compose/scripts/` now ships in the air-gap bundle

### What this fixes

v0.1.27 added a way to ship the **top-level** host-side scripts
(`backup.sh`, `restore.sh`, `update.sh`, `install.sh`, etc.) inside the
`.adcupdate` bundle. v0.1.28 fixed a critical air-gap install bug by
adding a `--packages-json` flag to `record-versions.sh` — but
`record-versions.sh` lives in `compose/scripts/`, a sibling directory the
bundle wasn't touching. So customers who installed v0.1.28 still had the
old `record-versions.sh` on disk and had to manually copy the new one in.

v0.1.29 extends the bundle to ship `compose/scripts/` too, with its own
whitelist of customer-runtime helpers (`record-versions.sh`,
`first-run.sh`, `generate-mqtt-certs.sh`, `generate-ssl.sh`, and the
`adc-*` shortcuts). Vendor-side build tooling that lives in the same
directory (`build-adcupdate-bundle.sh`, `build-packages-json.py`,
`sign-update-manifest.sh`) is deliberately excluded — those run only in
the release CI and have no business on a customer's host.

### Why it matters

From v0.1.29 onwards, any future fix to `record-versions.sh` or other
compose-side helpers will reach customers through the normal
**Install from file** path — no `scp` required, no out-of-band steps.
Previous copies are snapshotted to `compose/scripts/.previous-<timestamp>/`
so a regression can be rolled back by `cp -r`.

### Internal note

This is the symmetric counterpart to the existing `scripts/.previous-*`
snapshot behavior that v0.1.27 introduced. Both apply paths now use a
shared helper function instead of duplicated inline logic, so future
script-shipping additions only need a whitelist entry.

### Upgrade

Standard install through the Updates page → **Install from file** with
the v0.1.29 `.adcupdate`. No data changes, no schema migrations.
